description: Cancelling a leave request that is still in the Requested state credits back days that were never deducted, driving used_days negative and inflating the employee's balance (app/routes.py:95-99, cancel_request). Balance is only deducted on approval, but cancel_request restores unconditionally after any successful transition to Cancelled.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Log in as an employee whose Annual balance is total_days=20, used_days=0. 2. Submit a 5-day Annual leave request; it is stored with status 'Requested' and no balance is deducted. 3. Without any admin action, POST /cancel/<request_id>. 4. Query leave_balance for (employee, 'Annual').
expected: used_days remains 0 and remaining_days remains 20. No deduction was ever made for a Requested leave, so no restore is due.
actual: used_days = -5 and remaining_days = 25. The employee gains 5 days that were never entitled. The cycle can be repeated to inflate the balance without limit.

description: Approval does not re-validate the remaining balance, so several pending requests that each pass eligibility individually can all be approved and collectively exceed the entitlement (app/routes.py:123-126, approve_request). Eligibility is checked only at submission time, when nothing has been deducted yet.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Employee with Annual balance total_days=20, used_days=0. 2. Submit a 20-day Annual request (passes eligibility, status Requested, nothing deducted). 3. Submit a second 20-day Annual request; it also passes eligibility because remaining_days is still 20. 4. Log in as admin and approve both requests from /admin. 5. Query leave_balance for (employee, 'Annual').
expected: The second approval is refused with an insufficient-balance message; used_days never exceeds total_days and remaining_days never goes below 0.
actual: Both requests are approved. used_days = 40 against total_days = 20, remaining_days = -20. The employee is granted double their annual entitlement.

description: check_eligibility accepts a boolean as days_requested because bool is a subclass of int in Python, so isinstance(True, int) is True and True >= 1 (app/business_logic.py:49). A boolean is silently accepted as a one-day request instead of being rejected as an invalid type.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Call check_eligibility(employee, 'Annual', True, False, get_balance_func) directly with a service-eligible employee and a sufficient balance. 2. Inspect the returned tuple. 3. Repeat with days_requested=False.
expected: (False, 'Days requested must be at least 1') for both True and False. A boolean is not a valid day count and the type guard should reject it.
actual: days_requested=True returns (True, 'Eligible') and is processed as a 1-day request. Only False is rejected, and then for the wrong reason (False < 1 rather than wrong type).

description: calculate_service_months undercounts by one month when the hire day-of-month does not exist in the evaluation month (app/business_logic.py:13-14). The guard 'if today.day < hire_date.day: months -= 1' does not account for short months, so a 31st hire date never reaches its anniversary in a 28, 29 or 30-day month.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Create an employee with hire_date '2024-08-31'. 2. Evaluate calculate_service_months('2024-08-31') on 2025-02-28 (patch date.today()). 3. Compare against the calendar anniversary, which falls on the last day of February.
expected: 6 months. The six-month anniversary of a 31st hire date falls on the last day of a shorter month, so the employee is eligible on 2025-02-28.
actual: 5 months. check_eligibility then rejects the request with 'Minimum 6 months of service required. Current: 5 months', blocking an employee who is in fact eligible. The same undercount hits any hire date of the 29th to 31st.

description: The 'Taken' state is unreachable. LeaveRequest.VALID_TRANSITIONS declares Approved -> Taken (app/models.py:65), but no route, scheduled job, admin action or template anywhere in app/ ever calls update_status('Taken'), so a documented terminal state can never be entered.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Run: grep -rn \Taken\" app/ --include=*.py --include=*.html. 2. Observe the only three hits are the declarations in models.py (VALID_STATUSES
expected: VALID_TRANSITIONS key and value); no caller exists. 3. Approve a leave request and let its end date pass; re-read the request status."
actual: An approved leave request moves to 'Taken' once its leave period has elapsed, via an admin action or a scheduled transition, so completed leave is distinguishable from upcoming approved leave.
severity: The request stays 'Approved' indefinitely. 'Taken' is dead configuration: the state machine defines a transition the application never exercises, and reporting cannot distinguish taken from pending-future leave.

description: Integration test (test_def001) confirms that cancelling a Requested-state leave via the /cancel route drives remaining_days to 25 (was 20) because LeaveBalance.restore() is called unconditionally before the 'was_approved' guard was added. Reproduced at integration layer by Eyob Kassaye (Person 3) during test_integration.py authoring.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Run: pytest tests/test_integration.py::TestDefectReproducers::test_def001_cancel_requested_does_not_restore_balance -v. 2. Observe AssertionError: balance should be 20 after cancelling a Requested leave, got 25.
expected: remaining_days == 20 after cancelling a Requested leave.
actual: remaining_days == 25 — balance incorrectly restored. Confirmed at integration layer.

description: Integration test (test_def002) confirms that two 20-day Annual leave requests can both be approved when the entitlement is 20 days, resulting in used_days=40. The re-check inside approve_request does not fire because both requests were in Requested state simultaneously and no deduction had yet occurred at approval time. Reproduced at integration layer by Eyob Kassaye (Person 3) during test_integration.py authoring.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Run: pytest tests/test_integration.py::TestDefectReproducers::test_def002_second_approval_blocked_by_balance_check -v. 2. Observe AssertionError: used_days should not exceed total_days (20), got 40.
expected: used_days == 20 after both approval attempts (second blocked by balance check).
actual: used_days == 40 — both approved, employee granted double entitlement.
